- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward to account for potential rebound or policy-driven support.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >65), overshooting by 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to counteract underestimation.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply +1–3% adjustment to forecast mean if sentiment variance >0.3.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings, model often misjudges direction; favor mid-range or slightly downward bias unless sentiment is clearly bullish.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.25–0.75), model often drifts toward historical mean; use 30-day moving average as anchor for correction.
